spark.scene: True-color satellite view of the main Hawaiian Islands with dark ocean and scattered to extensive white cumulus and frontal clouds, heaviest to the west and south. The large southeastern island is partly cloudy with a pale linear feature trailing southwest from its southern part over the ocean.

evidence: Both volcanoes were non-erupting at image time: Kilauea ADVISORY/YELLOW paused, not erupting; Mauna Loa NORMAL/GREEN, not erupting, arguing against active vog emission. [E1]
No FIRMS fire clusters in the Hawaii domain on 2026-09-03; only Kilauea-summit volcanic thermal glow was returned, so no wildfire source supports smoke. [E6]

Measured drift toward 249 deg at ~12.5 km/h with good fit R2 0.84 agrees within ~24 deg of wind-blown-toward direction (from 93 deg => toward ~273 deg), consistent with a wind-advected cloud band. [E4, E5]
Inferred source end at 19.055N, -155.585E is 50.3 km from Kilauea summit and 46.8 km from Mauna Loa summit, not anchored at either vent as expected for a fresh vog plume. [E4]

137-km elongated oceanic streak with land fraction only 0.022 over ocean southwest of Hawaii Island, forming part of the extensive southern cloud field rather than a vent-rooted plume and without island-swallowing mask artifact. [E2, E3]

evidence_cited.text: Both volcanoes were non-erupting at image time: Kilauea ADVISORY/YELLOW paused, not erupting; Mauna Loa NORMAL/GREEN, not erupting, arguing against active vog emission.
No FIRMS fire clusters in the Hawaii domain on 2026-09-03; only Kilauea-summit volcanic thermal glow was returned, so no wildfire source supports smoke.
Measured drift toward 249 deg at ~12.5 km/h with good fit R2 0.84 agrees within ~24 deg of wind-blown-toward direction (from 93 deg => toward ~273 deg), consistent with a wind-advected cloud band.
Inferred source end at 19.055N, -155.585E is 50.3 km from Kilauea summit and 46.8 km from Mauna Loa summit, not anchored at either vent as expected for a fresh vog plume.

137-km elongated oceanic streak with land fraction only 0.022 over ocean southwest of Hawaii Island, forming part of the extensive southern cloud field rather than a vent-rooted plume and without island-swallowing mask artifact.

classify.caveats: Single faint streak in partly cloudy scene; motion agrees with wind but direction alone cannot separate thin cloud from dilute haze. Both volcanoes officially non-erupting and no FIRMS fires were found, so volcanic or smoke origin is unlikely but a very thin residual haze mixed with cloud cannot be fully excluded.

kilauea.activity_summary: Kīlauea volcano is not erupting; the summit eruption in Halemaʻumaʻu is paused. Summit reinflation has increased over the past day. A forecast window of September 7-12 is likely for the next fountain episode.

mauna_loa.activity_summary: Mauna Loa earthquake counts decreased in July, while the summit region showed patterns of slight inflation. Mauna Loa had a decrease in seismic activity compared to the previous month; a total of 57 earthquakes were detected in Mauna Loa's summit region during the July reporting period, after 94 in June. Most earthquakes occurred deep beneath the upper Southwest Rift Zone or broadly scattered around the upper flanks.
